main_text.head: IN D. IACOBI AV-berti Medicinæ Doctoris celeberri-mi, Physici præstantissimi, institutio-nes physicas Mosis Molerij Epigramma.

p.i: Multos[?] astra juvat, terrásq. errasse per omnes, Lustrasse & vasto quicquid in Oceano: At vero abstrusas rerum cognoscere causas, Non datur in tanto cuique natâre freto.

Ergo (lector) ades, quid cælū, terra, quid unda, Et quis res atomos, spiritus intus alat, Quæ sit natura vis atque innata facultas, Et quæ sint animæ munera iusta tuæ, Has tibi divitias, thesauros atque latentes Subtili Aubertus dexteritate dabit.
Ille tibi physices claros ita sarrijt[?] hortos, Ut nullus possit sentibus esse locus.
Hæc igitur grata doctissima dogmata fronte Suscipito, & vigili volue, revolue[?] manu.

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "Multos" (first letters obscured by a flourish); "sarrijt" (word run together with "ita" in print, reading uncertain); "revolue" (the printed letter could be n, not u). The printed ampersand is a special form, transcribed as &. The Greek-letter ornament before "Aubertus" in line 6 of the second stanza is a printer's mark and is not transcribed. Faint show-through from the reverse page is ignored.
